extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, practitioners, examiners, and public users performing USPTO prior-art searches
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting prior-art searches using the USPTO Patent Public Search (PPUBS) / PE2E tools and applying search results to drafting. Covers search capabilities, strategies, examiner workflow insights, and drafting implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-specific searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Search by discrete bibliographic and content fields: inventor name; assignee name; application number / publication number; classification (CPC, IPC, USPC); claim text; specification text; date ranges; priority dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use fielded searches to target documents precisely (e.g., search claim text vs. specification). Combine field searches to narrow results to specific applicants, classifications, or time windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean operators and search syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for standard Boolean operators AND, OR, NOT; phrase searching with quotes; wildcard characters (* for stem, ? for single character); proximity operators (NEAR, ADJ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Boolean logic, phrases, wildcards, and proximity operators to refine and control result sets; use quotes for exact phrases and wildcards for stemming; proximity operators help find terms appearing close together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to search by patent classification schemes: CPC (Cooperative Patent Classification), IPC (International Patent Classification), USPC (legacy U.S. classification, pre-2013), and F-terms (Japan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with relevant classifications to capture the core technical area; use co-classification combinations and classification hierarchies to broaden or narrow searches. Be aware of legacy vs. current classification systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define search concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the main technical concepts of the invention and develop synonyms for each concept, considering both technical and lay terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list concepts and synonyms before searching to ensure breadth and to avoid missing prior art that uses different terminology; include alternate spellings and domain-specific jargon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative search approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Start broad with classifications, narrow with keywords, and refine searches based on initial results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat searching as an iterative process: use broad classification pulls to map the space, then add keywords and filters to home in on the most relevant references; repeat cycles to refine coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple search strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a mix of approaches: classification searching, keyword searching, citation analysis (forward and backward), inventor and assignee searches, and co-classification combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No single strategy is sufficient — combine approaches to improve recall and precision. For example, use inventor/assignee searches to find portfolios and citation trails to find influential references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document your search
rubrics_metrics.description: Save search strategies, note databases searched, record search dates, and track relevant results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve search histories and metadata (which databases, dates, and query strings) for reproducibility, file-wrapper support, and quality review. Use the tool's save/search tagging features where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool features that support effective searching
rubrics_metrics.description: PPUBS/PE2E provides free online remote searching, multiple layouts and tools, multi-color highlighting, document tagging into multiple groups, adding notes to images with tags, and saving/tagging searches and patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage highlighting, tagging, and note features to organize results, collaborate, and document why references were selected; use multiple layouts to view full text and images efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation analysis (forward and backward)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze citations to and from a patent (backward references cited by a document and forward references citing it) to identify relevant prior art chains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use citation trails to find earlier foundational references and later related work; combine citation analysis with keyword and classification searches for comprehensive coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emulate examiner workflow practices
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO examiners search prior art using classification + keyword combinations, build search histories that become part of the file wrapper, identify references for office action rejections, and document search efforts for quality review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand and mimic examiner search patterns (classification + keyword combos, thorough documentation) to anticipate what examiners will find and to prepare defensible search records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting informed by search patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: When drafting applications, use technical terminology examiners are likely to find, include synonyms in claim language, consider classification placement when drafting, and anticipate which references examiners will likely cite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use insights from prior-art searches to shape claim language and specification wording (include synonyms and classification-relevant terms) to improve discoverability and reduce avoidable citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage complementary external tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use other free tools (Google Patents, Espacenet, WIPO PatentScope, Lens.org, DEPATISnet) and commercial platforms (Derwent Innovation, PatentSight, Questel Orbit, Minesoft PatBase, LexisNexis Patent Optimizer) to complement USPTO searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different tools offer varied coverage and features (e.g., global coverage, citation analytics, academic integration). Cross-check across tools to improve recall and gather additional metadata or analytics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and resource utilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Make use of USPTO-provided training materials, quick reference guides, FAQs, help center, Public Search Facility, and Patent and Trademark Resource Centers (PTRCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access official training and help resources (including contacting psf@uspto.gov) to learn tool-specific features, advanced techniques, and local help at PTRCs for hands-on assistance.
